methodological_questions: Does a PULL_UP possession following a failed PNR show lift over a within-unit baseline in at least 70% of units?
Is the median unit lift above 2pp, and in which metric (PPP, make rate, or EFG)?
How should a 'unit' be defined (defense team, offense team, team-season, or defender-PT cell), and what baseline should lift be measured against?
Are derived PNR and PULL_UP labels reliable enough, and is the per-unit sample large enough, to support a league-wide test?

historical_evidence.finding: Shot-level 2024-25 PNR share of half-court shots ranged from about 7.6% (OKC) and 7.9% (BOS) to 13.8% (IND). The record notes that calibrated possession-level PNR is about 17.9-19.6%, and that the rates are a calibration input with no pass/fail gate.

Across 870 ordered team pairs, exploitable defensive PT edges (>=+5% vs league) appeared for 33.3% of pairs and traps for 23.3%. The record notes that edges depend only on the defense (e.g., DAL PNR +9.2% for every offense), so they are not matchup-specific.

Pre-game play-type PPP rankings from training data correlated with held-out efficiency (median rho +0.539; top-3 median hit 100%; median lift +0.4261 PPP). The record caveats that top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency PTs (CUT, PUTBACK, TRANSITION), and 10.5% of rows had rho<0.

On-ball coverage labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) were confidently assigned to 14.9% of DET possessions and 3.3% of ORL possessions (n=67/60 on-ball possessions). The switches_on field was not populated by the NBA matchups feed.

No opponent-specific edge was detected in the ORL-DET decomposition: all top openers were 'universal only' (opponent-specific share +1.4% to +6.9%), and DET was within +/-5% of league on all seeded PTs.

Adapters toward SHOULD counters showed a PPP advantage of +0.058 to +0.060 across repeated runs (e.g., APPM-013 p=0.0199). The record lists the limitation as selection or regression to the mean; the SWITCH subgroup reversed.
Falsification T3 found no PPP carryover of an in-game adapter lift to Game N+1 (negative mix-carry). The record is classed as B_powered_null, though sample size is recorded as NOT_RECORDED.

Equilibrium and actual-mix matchup predictors had negative R2 (-0.1981 and -0.7167) on 520 holdout cells (69,876 possessions), while the team-offense mean had R2 +0.1197. The record shows the model-based counter predictors failing against simple means (verdict tool_eval_fail).

Player-channel matchup lifts were large on small cells (e.g., Banchero on Huerter SPOT_UP +8.4pp with n_def=17), while team-PT lifts were small (ORL vs DET PNR +1.2pp). Cell n was often 15-54 and the record flags exposure sparsity.

TOV-force lifts shrank by about 50% or more after opponent re-routing and counter checks (e.g., ORL +8.4 to +3.7pp). The record is descriptive, on 4 games and 8 offense-defense sides, with net lift described as model-implied rather than observed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Equilibrium and actual-mix matchup predictors for counter-PPP lift, compared with simple team and league means.
failed_approaches.why: Both predictors had negative holdout R2 while the team-offense mean was positive (+0.1197). The record classes this as B_powered_null, and the lambda sweep worsened monotonically.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling on-ball defensive schemes (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from the NBA matchups feed to define counter conditions.
failed_approaches.why: Label rates were very low (14.9% for DET, 3.3% for ORL), switches_on was unpopulated, and the record lists label error and small sample as limitations.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player-channel matchup decomposition as evidence for counter lift.
failed_approaches.why: Cell n of 15-28 defensive possessions, primary-defender attribution that included helper steals, and no holdout or game-outcome check. The record classes this as A_unanswerable with LIM:insufficient_exposure.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Three-ply adversarial survival of raw turnover-force lifts under opponent re-route and counter checks.
failed_approaches.why: Lifts shrank by about 50% or more, the net lift was model-implied rather than observed, and the record reports no validation and a mechanism recorded as E_unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-game adaptation toward SHOULD counters as evidence of counter effectiveness.
failed_approaches.why: Adapter advantage was attributed to selection or regression to the mean, and the SWITCH subgroup reversed sign.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Cross-game carryover of an in-game adapter PPP lift.
failed_approaches.why: No carryover replicated at Game N+1 (T3, negative mix-carry), so in-game lift was not shown to persist across games.

evidence_establishes: Single-cell and single-game counter or matchup lifts in this project's records shrank substantially or failed when re-tested, under holdout, falsification, or additional checks (SF-APPA-067, SF-APPA-066, SF13, SF-CHT-020).

Defensive PT edges in this project's records were largely defender-driven and not matchup-specific (SF-APPA-034, SF-APPM-012), which means a league-wide unit-level PULL_UP lift could reflect defensive or offensive identity rather than the counter itself.
Derived labels were a recorded weak point. Coverage labels were sparse or unreliable (SF-APPS-058), and PNR rates depend on a calibration from a proxy (SF-APPM-058).
Play-type PPP rankings have modest out-of-sample validity but are partly driven by league-wide high-efficiency PTs (SF-APPA-063), so a lift above baseline needs a within-PT or within-unit comparison.
evidence_does_not_establish: None of the retrieved records tests PNR fail followed by PULL_UP as a counter, or reports a unit-level lift distribution for PULL_UP. The question is therefore not answered by the historical evidence.
The retrieved records do not define a unit, a PNR-fail label, or a PULL_UP label that matches this question, so they do not show whether the 70% and 2pp thresholds are achievable.
No retrieved record reports a PNR-fail-conditional baseline for PULL_UP, so the expected size of lift or its variance is unknown.
The retrieved records do not cover the 2025-26 playoffs or the complete 2025-26 regular season, so temporal stability for this question is unknown.
own_inferences: The threshold 'lift > 0 in >=70% of units' is only meaningful if units are defined independently of the outcome. With 30 teams, 70% corresponds to at least 21 units, so the test is coarse and sensitive to unit definition.
The metric for '2pp' is ambiguous: percentage points of make rate, EFG, or PPP would imply different scales and thresholds.
A league-wide median lift could be driven by high-volume units. Median across units without weighting may be unstable where PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP counts are small.
uncertainties: Whether the PNR-fail label (defined as a turnover, a missed shot, or no score) and the PULL_UP label are derivable from the play-by-play sub-type fields without the derived graph layer, which the records did not check.
Sample sizes per unit for the PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP sequence across 2022-23 to 2025-26 are not reported in any retrieved record.
Whether the 2025-26 partial season data changes eligibility, given it is only complete from 2026-04-13 (regular season) and 2026-06-21 (playoffs).
Whether PULL_UP's lift is confounded by shot quality, shooter identity, defender quality, or PT mix, none of which the retrieved records addressed.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval found no direct test of the question, but it did show that similar counter and matchup lifts in this project shrank, failed holdout checks, or were attributed to selection, regression to the mean, or defender-level effects (SF-APPA-067, SF13, SF-APPA-020, SF-APPA-034). That moved the decision from a straightforward test to proceed_with_changes: the test must use within-unit baselines, a holdout period, placebo actions, and pre-registered unit and label definitions, and should not present a small-cell lift as a counter.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR-fail and PULL_UP labels come from play-by-play and a derived graph layer; the labels must be checked against raw sub-type fields, since calibrated PNR rates in SF-APPM-058 depend on a proxy.
Per-unit counts of PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP sequences are likely small, comparable to the 15-54 cell sizes that SF-APPA-066 flagged as insufficient.
Power for detecting a median lift of 2pp across units has not been computed; with 30 units, the 70% criterion is coarse.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests PNR fail followed by PULL_UP as a league-wide counter. Related work shows that counter and matchup lifts in this project were often small, unstable across cells, or null on holdout. Derived labels for coverage and PNR were weak. The question is therefore open, but the related evidence is cautionary.

risks.text: PNR-fail and PULL_UP are defined from derived play-type records, so the outcome label is partly a product of the same pipeline that generates the possession groupings.
The 2pp threshold is undefined in metric terms (make rate, EFG, or PPP). The unit-level lift measure may not be reliable at per-unit sample sizes.
The 70% and median 2pp criteria are not powered at a per-unit level without a pre-computed sample and variance.
Small per-unit PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP counts, as seen in player-channel cells of 15-54, may give unstable lifts.
Selecting PULL_UP as a counter after seeing PNR-fail outcomes would produce regression to the mean, as in the SF13 adapter artifact.
Baseline PPP and shot-type mix differ by unit; a lift that ignores baseline PT efficiency can look positive by construction, as in the PT-rank caveat in SF-APPA-063.

Defender quality, shooter identity, shot quality, and possession context (time, score, fouls) may drive PULL_UP outcomes after a failed PNR, and SF-APPA-034 shows that defender-driven edges are not matchup-specific.
Testing PULL_UP against many PNR-fail variants and multiple metrics without correction inflates the chance of a spurious league-wide pass.
Without a placebo action (non-counter after PNR fail), a positive lift cannot be separated from a generic after-PNR effect.
Play-type efficiency has drifted over seasons (SF-APPA-063 caveat), and 2025-26 is partial before the complete dates, so pooling across seasons may mix regimes.
Derived PNR labels may misclassify possessions, and the coverage-label records show low and unreliable label rates.

design.estimand: Within-unit difference in points per possession (primary) between PULL_UP and a matched non-counter action on possessions following a failed PNR, with make rate and EFG as secondary metrics. Lift is in PPP units; 2pp is interpreted as 0.02 PPP and the interpretation must be pre-registered.
design.unit: Defensive team (30 units) for the primary test. Offensive team and team-season are secondary units. Unit definitions must be fixed before analysis.
design.sample: Complete regular seasons 2022-23 through 2024-25 for discovery, and complete 2025-26 regular season (from 2026-04-13) as the holdout. Playoffs are excluded from the primary test. Partial 2025-26 data is excluded.
design.power: Compute the minimum detectable median lift and the probability of at least 21 of 30 units showing positive lift, using a simulation based on observed PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP counts per unit. Pre-register the minimum count per unit (e.g., 30 possessions) below which a unit is excluded and reported separately.
design.controls: Compare PULL_UP against a matched non-counter action on the same offense and the same defense in the same game state (score, period, time remaining). Adjust for shooter identity, shot distance, defender matchup, and PT base rate. Use within-unit baselines, not league means.
design.falsification: Run the same lift calculation for placebo actions (e.g., a non-counter action after PNR fail) and for shuffled PNR-fail labels within game. The primary result is not supported if placebo lifts are of similar size.
design.multiplicity: Single pre-registered primary test (21 of 30 units positive and median lift above the threshold). Secondary metrics and unit definitions are corrected with Holm adjustment.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if (a) at least 21 of 30 units show positive lift on the discovery seasons and the holdout 2025-26 regular season, (b) the median unit lift exceeds 0.02 PPP with a bootstrap 95% CI whose lower bound is above 0, and (c) placebo lifts are not comparable in size. Otherwise report as rejected (adequately powered null), uncertain, or artifact as appropriate.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, substitution, and matchup files for 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and the complete 2025-26 regular season (from 2026-04-13). Derived play-type graph records must be version-locked and validated against raw sub-type fields before use.

methodological_questions: Does PULL_UP shot after PNR fail yield lift over baseline in at least 70% of units?
Is median lift above 2 percentage points across units?
What unit definition and baseline are appropriate for counter-strategy lift?
How sensitive are conclusions to sample size, exposure, and derived labels?
args.query: PNR fail followed by PULL_UP counter lift league-wide units median lift defensive suppression counter strategy

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
